name: retrocore
description: 6502 and Z80 assembly and BASIC with source-level debugging on emulated Apple II family computers and the TRS-80 Model I.

scripts.test:grammar: node scripts/generate-grammar.mjs --check && node scripts/generate-basic-grammar.mjs --check && node --test out/test/grammar.test.js out/test/basicGrammar.test.js out/test/pascalGrammar.test.js out/test/display.test.js out/test/pictures.test.js out/test/hardware.test.js out/test/machines.test.js out/test/startFlow.test.js
scripts.test: npm run compile && npm run test:grammar && npm run test:editor

retrocore.languageServer.enabled.description: Run the retrocore language server: errors as you type, go to definition, hover, completion and symbols.

retrocore.languageServer.host.description: Path to Retrocore.Debug.dll. Empty uses the workspace build under artifacts/AnyCPU/Release/Retrocore.Debug/net10.0.

retrocore.basic.dialect.markdownDescription: The BASIC of a `.bas` file with no `REM retrocore` pragma and no dialect extension (such as `.applesoft.bas`). Empty uses the BASIC of the machine being debugged.

enumDescriptions: Keeps the machine's panel, dimmed, with Restart, Start Machine and Close.
Closes the machine's panel.
retrocore.display.onSessionEnd.markdownDescription: What the machine's display panel does when its debug session ends.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No machine is running.
[Start Machine](command:retrocore.startMachine)
Or pick a machine under Retrocore in the Run and Debug dropdown and press F5.

Start a retro machine without a launch.json: the Apple II family or the TRS-80 Model I.
[Start Retro Machine](command:retrocore.startMachine)

commands.title: Retrocore: Save Last Machine as Launch Configuration

enumDescriptions: The Apple II family; model says which.
The Apple III.
The TRS-80 Model I.
The Apple-1, with the Woz Monitor and the Apple Cassette Interface.
The TRS-80 Color Computer 1, 2 or 3; model says which.
The older name for apple2, from when only the IIe was emulated.
machine.description: The machine to emulate: apple2 is the Apple II family (model picks the IIe or enhanced IIe), apple3 an Apple III, trs80-model1 a TRS-80 Model I, apple1 an Apple-1, and coco a TRS-80 Color Computer (model picks 1, 2 or 3).

romDirectory.description: Directory of externally supplied ROM dumps; defaults to RETROCORE_IIE_ROMS for the IIe, RETROCORE_IIPLUS_ROMS for the II Plus, RETROCORE_II_ROMS for the II, RETROCORE_APPLE3_ROMS for the Apple III (MAME's apple3 set), RETROCORE_TRS80_ROMS for the Model I, RETROCORE_APPLE1_ROMS for the Apple-1 (wozmon.bin and aci.bin) and RETROCORE_COCO_ROMS for the Color Computer. Without dumps the ROMs are assembled from the SDK's sources, which are byte-identical to them, but for the CoCo 3's, which needs its dump: the Color Computer's are under MAME's names (coco3.rom, and extbas11.rom or disk11.rom to replace the sources'), in the directory or its coco, coco2b, coco3 and coco_fdc folders.

highRam.description: Apple-1: a 4 KB bank of RAM at $E000-$EFFF, where BASIC loads and runs.

cassetteInterface.description: Apple-1: the Apple Cassette Interface in the expansion slot, started from the Monitor with C100R.

rom.description: Model I: Level II or Level I BASIC.

revision.description: Model I: the Level II revision; 1.3 reads the dumps' _alt parts.

ramKilobytes.description: Model I: RAM in kilobytes, 4-48; defaults to 48 with the Expansion Interface, else 16 (4 for Level I). Apple II and II Plus: 16, 32 or 48 (the default) on the board. Apple III: 128, 256 (the default) or 512. Apple-1: 4 (the default) or 8 from $0000. Color Computer 1 and 2: 4, 16, 32 or 64 (16 on a CoCo 1, 64 on a CoCo 2); CoCo 3: 128 (the default) or 512.

expansionInterface.description: Model I: the Expansion Interface (RAM above 16K, the clock interrupt, disks); defaults on for Level II.

anyOf.description: Model I: the Expansion Interface's disk controller; defaults on when disks are given, since with a controller and no disk the ROM waits for one. Color Computer: the disk controller cartridge with Disk Extended Color BASIC; defaults on when disks are given.

enumDescriptions: IIe: the Disk II in slot 6, the default for WOZ and DOS-order images, and with diskBootRom.
IIe: the slot 7 block device, the default for .po images.

diskController.description: Model I: true or false, whether the Expansion Interface has its disk controller (on by default when disks are given). Color Computer: true or false, whether the disk controller cartridge is in the slot (on by default when disks are given). IIe: diskII or slot7, where diskImage goes (the Disk II in slot 6, or the slot 7 block device for .po images).

lowercase.description: Model I: the lowercase modification's seventh video bit. Color Computer 1 and 2: the MC6847T1 VDG, which shows lowercase, as on the CoCo 2B.

characterGenerator.description: Model I: the font: the stock MCM6670P, or Radio Shack's lowercase kit's replacement (as xtrs reconstructs it); defaults to kit with lowercase.

snow.description: Model I: show video snow when the CPU reads or writes video RAM while the beam draws.

doubler.description: Model I: a double-density doubler: percom (selected by $FE/$FF commands, as NEWDOS/80 expects), tandy (the Radio Shack doubler, selected by $80/$A0 sector writes) or both.

cassette.description: Model I and Color Computer: a .cas tape to play. Apple-1: a .wav tape, which plays from the start of the session.

fastCassette.description: Model I and Color Computer: run as fast as possible while the cassette motor runs, so tapes load and save quickly. Apple-1: the same while a tape plays or records. The machine's own timing is unchanged.

disks.description: Model I: JV1 or JV3 (.jv3) images for drives 0-3. Apple III: DOS- or ProDOS-order (.po) or WOZ images for .D1, the built-in drive, then .D2-.D4. Color Computer: JVC (.dsk) images for drives 0-3, which put the disk controller in the slot.

bootSeconds.description: Model I and Color Computer: emulated seconds the ROM runs before a program loads, to set up its RAM; defaults to 1 on a Model I and 2 on a Color Computer when loading a program.

controllers.description: Apple II: read game controllers (Xbox, PlayStation and others) into the game port while the machine runs, even with VS Code in the background. The first controller's left stick or d-pad is the joystick (paddles 0 and 1) and its A, B and X buttons are buttons 0, 1 and 2; a second controller is paddles 2 and 3. False leaves the paddles unconnected.

programmersAid.description: Apple II: put Programmer's Aid #1 in the II's D0 socket ($D000-$D7FF), from the romDirectory's dump if it is there and otherwise built from the SDK's source. CALL -12288 starts its hi-res graphics. Other models have no D0 socket.

fastDisk.description: IIe and Apple III: run as fast as possible while any disk drive's motor turns, then return to the chosen speed. The machine runs the same cycles either way; only how fast they pass in real time changes. The display panel's Fast disk changes it while debugging.

enumDescriptions: The machine's real speed.
Twice the machine's clock.
Four times the machine's clock.
Eight times the machine's clock.
As fast as the host can run it.
speed.description: How fast the machine runs, as a multiple of its clock; the display panel's Speed changes it while debugging.

enumDescriptions: No sound, and no cost.
The IIe's speaker, in mono. Costs about 2% of emulation speed. On a Color Computer, its sound through the TV: the DAC, cassette and single-bit sound.

The speaker and the Mockingboard's two sound chips, in stereo, and the Mockingboard in slot 4 unless mockingboard is false. Slows emulation by about a quarter, because the chips' output is worked out every cycle.
sound.description: IIe and Color Computer: what the display panel plays while the machine runs. Sound plays in time only at the machine's real speed (speed 1); the panel's Sound button changes it while debugging.

mockingboard.description: IIe: whether the Mockingboard is in slot 4. Off unless sound is mockingboard; the Retro Devices view's Add Card puts it in while debugging.

enumDescriptions: A color monitor or television (the default on the Apple II family, the Apple III and the Color Computer).
A black and white monochrome monitor: on an Apple II, every dot sharp, as double hi-res desktops need.
A green-phosphor monochrome monitor.
An amber-phosphor monochrome monitor.
screen.description: The monitor the video is shown on: color on the Apple II family, the Apple III and the Color Computer, or a white, green or amber monochrome one on any machine (green is the default on the Apple-1 and the Model I, which have no color). The display panel's Screen menu changes it, and its choice is kept for later launches on machines that have it.

mouse.description: Apple II: the slot of an AppleMouse II-compatible mouse card, which a click on the display drives until Escape. None by default; the Retro Devices view's Add Card puts it in while debugging.

logpointLimit.description: The most lines logpoints write to the Debug Console each second; the rest are counted and reported. 0 lifts the limit.

diskImage.description: Disk image for drive 1: a .po image goes to the slot 7 block device, and a WOZ, .dsk or .do image to the Disk II in slot 6.

dos.description: Boots the program from a fresh DOS disk built from the SDK's DOS sources (3.2 uses the 13-sector Disk II): the program as a binary file and a HELLO that BRUNs it, in a Disk II in slot 6. The program must start at its first address.

dosYear.description: With dos 3.3, which DOS 3.3 to boot: 1983 (the 680-0210-A System Master's) or 1980 (the 680-0051 masters').

diskSectors.description: Without diskBootRom, the Disk II's ROMs are assembled from the SDK's sources: the 16-sector card's (341-0027 and 341-0028) or the 13-sector card's (341-0009 and 341-0010).

diskBootRom.description: Externally supplied 256-byte Disk II P5/P5A boot ROM, instead of the SDK's; selects native floppy I/O.

diskSequencerRom.description: Externally supplied 256-byte Disk II P6 sequencer PROM.

sequencerLayout.description: Explicit sequencer ROM pin/table layout: boot-socket for a dump read from the boot ROM's socket, as the known 341-0010 dump is.

enumDescriptions: The enhanced Apple IIe: a 65C02, MouseText and the enhanced firmware.
The original (unenhanced) Apple IIe: an NMOS 6502.
The Apple II Plus: AppleSoft and the Autostart Monitor, an NMOS 6502, 48 KB and a language card in slot 0.
The Apple II: Integer BASIC and the original Monitor (or, with monitor autostart, the Autostart Monitor), an NMOS 6502 and 48 KB.
The older name for iie-enhanced.
The older name for iie.
The Color Computer 1: Color BASIC with Extended Color BASIC, the MC6847 VDG and 16 KB.
The Color Computer 2: Color BASIC with Extended Color BASIC and 64 KB.
The Color Computer 3: Extended Color BASIC 2.0, the GIME and 128 KB.
model.description: Apple II: which model of the family. Color Computer: coco1, coco2 or coco3.

enumDescriptions: A language card: 16 KB of RAM at $D000-$FFFF, which DOS 3.3 loads the other BASIC into. The II Plus's default.
A firmware card with the other model's BASIC and Monitor in ROM: AppleSoft on a II, Integer BASIC on a II Plus. $C080 selects it and $C081 the board's ROM, as DOS 3.3's FP and INT do.
Nothing. The II's default.
slot0.description: Apple II and II Plus: the card in slot 0. The IIe's language card is built in.

enumDescriptions: The original Monitor: reset goes to the Monitor's * prompt; CONTROL-B starts Integer BASIC.
The Autostart Monitor of later IIs: power-on boots a disk or starts BASIC, and reset returns to BASIC.
Color Computer 3: a composite monitor or TV, the default.
Color Computer 3: the CM-8 RGB monitor, with the GIME's 64 colors as they are.
monitor.description: Apple II: its Monitor ROM. Color Computer 3: the monitor the GIME drives.

colorBasic.description: Color Computer 1 and 2: the Color BASIC ROM, bas10.rom to bas13.rom; 1.3 is the CoCo 2B's.

extendedBasic.description: Color Computer 1 and 2: the Extended Color BASIC ROM, extbas10.rom or extbas11.rom, or none; without dumps, built from the SDK's ExtendedBasic.asm.

diskBasic.description: Color Computer: the disk controller's Disk Extended Color BASIC ROM, disk10.rom or disk11.rom; without dumps, built from the SDK's DiskBasic.asm.

enumDescriptions: The colors most CoCo 1 and 2 machines show in 256-dot graphics, where RESET is pressed until they do.
The other phase.
Black and white dots, as on a monochrome monitor.
artifacts.description: Color Computer 1 and 2: the artifact colors a composite monitor shows in two-color graphics.

cartridge.description: Color Computer: a ROM pack image (.ccc or .rom, up to 16 KB) in the cartridge slot.

autostart.description: Color Computer: whether the ROM pack starts itself through the CART interrupt, as games do.

enumDescriptions: Revision 1 and later: six hi-res colors.
Revision 0, the first boards: hi-res ignores bit 7, so four colors: black, white, green and violet.

firmwareCardRoms.description: Apple II and II Plus: the folder of the other model's ROM dumps the slot 0 firmware card holds; by default RETROCORE_IIPLUS_ROMS or RETROCORE_II_ROMS, or its folder (APPLE II+ or APPLE II) beside romDirectory, and without dumps the SDK's sources of them.

source.description: Native, ca65 or Merlin source to assemble with retrocore and load; replaces program and debugFile.

dialect.description: Dialect of source; defaults to native unless the file's first-line pragma names one.

basic.description: A BASIC file to load and RUN: .applesoft.bas, .level2.bas, or a .bas whose first line names its dialect. Numbered lines, or lines with labels; the machine boots to BASIC's prompt first. Replaces source and program.

run.description: With basic: RUN the program once it is loaded; false leaves BASIC at its prompt.

debugFile.description: cc65 .dbg (from ld65 or Retrocore.Debug --assemble) or VICE labels for program.

loadAddress.description: Load address of program, or origin of source when no linker configuration places it; defaults to $6000 on the IIe and $7000 on the Model I.

entryAddress.description: Starting PC; defaults to the load address, or the first section of source.

checkContracts.description: When a call to a routine with a ;; Keeps: section returns with a kept register, flag or memory location changed: report it in the Debug Console (warn), also stop there (stop), or do not check (off). With warn, ticking the Breakpoints view's Routine broke its Keeps: promise filter also stops.

checkUses.description: Also report registers a routine changed that its ;; Uses:, Out: and Keeps: sections do not list.

sdkRoms.description: Directory of the SDK's ROM sources to debug instead of the copy beside the debug host, so breakpoints set in those files bind: the Apple II's Roms directory (Slot7.rom.asm, AppleSoft, System, IntegerBasic, DiskII, Dos), the Model I's (Level2.asm, Level1.asm, CharacterGenerator.asm), or the Color Computer's (ColorBasic.asm).

breakpoints.description: Breakpoints to add before launching, once each: a file with a 1-based line, a label in a file whose first instruction to stop at, or a function breakpoint on a label or address expression.

label.description: A label in path; the breakpoint is on its first instruction.

function.description: A function breakpoint instead: a label or address expression, such as DISPLAY_CHAR or $C600.

condition.description: An expression that must be nonzero to stop, such as A == $0D.

hitCondition.description: Which hits stop: N or =N the Nth, >N, >=N, <N, <=N, or %N every Nth.

logMessage.description: Log this instead of stopping; {expression} shows a value, {expression,d} in decimal and {expression,c} as a character.
